items.key_phrase: Write code a reader can follow in one pass.
items.look_at: `src/redirect.js` and any module it imports for the redirect decision
items.no_when: The trusted host is repeated as literals in several places, or the decision is spread across files or long branches a reviewer must piece together.
items.question: Is the trusted origin defined once as a named constant, and is the allow-or-fall-back decision made in `resolveRedirect` or a few small named helpers that a reviewer can read top to bottom?
items.yes_when: One named constant holds the trusted HTTPS host or origin, and the code that decides a target is safe sits in one short, readable place.

items.key_phrase: A condition that joins two or more checks with a logical and/or (`&&`, `||`, `and`, `or`) gets a name that says what it means in plain English
items.look_at: Conditions in `src/redirect.js`
items.no_when: A compound condition such as `url.protocol === "https:" && url.hostname === HOST` appears inline without a name.
items.question: Does each condition in the redirect code that joins two or more checks with `&&` or `||` have a name, as a predicate function or a named local, other than plain null or empty checks?
items.yes_when: Every compound condition is a named predicate or a named local, or there are none besides null and empty checks.

items.key_phrase: Horizontal layers exist only for a real boundary
items.look_at: New files and modules in the diff, and how the new behavior flows through them
items.no_when: One behavior is split across new pass-through layers that add no boundary.
items.question: Does NOT add a new layer (a service, repository, manager, or helper module) that the change's behavior passes through without a process, deploy, trust, persistence, or transport boundary or proven duplication?
items.yes_when: New modules sit at a real boundary or remove proven duplication, or the behavior stays in the module that owns the feature.

items.key_phrase: Add no route, command, flag, config key, environment variable, or startup requirement the request did not name
items.look_at: Routes, CLI definitions, config and environment reads, and startup code in the final workspace
items.no_when: The trusted host comes from an environment variable or a config file or key, or the change adds a route, command, flag, or startup requirement.
items.question: Does NOT add any route, command, flag, config key, environment variable, or startup requirement, including one for the trusted host? The task names none.
items.yes_when: No route, command, flag, config key, environment variable, or startup requirement was added, and the trusted host lives in the code. New exports do not count here.

items.key_phrase: Build only what the user asked for.
items.look_at: The behavior the diff adds, compared with the request
items.no_when: The change adds an allowlist of several hosts, a parameter or options object that lets callers choose the trusted host, wildcard or subdomain matching, logging or reporting of rejected targets, a thrown error instead of the `/` fallback, or rewrites accepted targets to a different path.
items.question: Does NOT add user-visible behavior beyond keeping same-site paths, accepting absolute HTTPS URLs on the one trusted host, and falling back to `/` for everything else?
items.yes_when: Every new behavior serves the request.

items.key_phrase: Ask before adding a dependency.
items.look_at: Package manifests and lockfiles in the diff
items.no_when: A new dependency appears that nobody approved.
items.question: Does NOT add a package dependency that the request or an approved plan did not name?
items.yes_when: No dependency was added, or each added one was named in the request or the approved plan.

items.key_phrase: Extract an abstraction only when code in more than one place serves the same purpose.
items.look_at: New interfaces, base classes, factories, and generic helpers in the diff, and their call sites
items.no_when: An abstraction has a single use or exists for flexibility nobody asked for.
items.question: Does NOT add an abstraction (an interface, base class, factory, or generic helper) that has only one use in the change?
items.yes_when: Each new abstraction serves more than one place that has the same purpose.

items.key_phrase: fail closed on auth, authz, validation, and crypto errors
items.look_at: `resolveRedirect` in `src/redirect.js` and any parse step it calls
items.no_when: Some failure returns the original target, rethrows to the caller, or lets an unchecked value through.
items.question: When the target cannot be parsed, is not a string, or parsing throws, does `resolveRedirect` return `/` rather than the target?
items.yes_when: Every parse failure, exception, and non-string input leads to the `/` fallback.

items.key_phrase: Deny by default
items.look_at: The accept and reject branches in `src/redirect.js`
items.no_when: The code rejects specific bad patterns (such as `//`, `javascript:`, or a list of hosts) and returns anything else, or matches the host with `includes`, `endsWith`, `startsWith`, or a prefix check on the raw string.
items.question: Does `resolveRedirect` return a target only when it is a same-site path or an `https:` URL whose parsed host exactly equals the trusted host, falling back to `/` for everything else, rather than blocking a list of known-bad patterns?
items.yes_when: Acceptance needs a positive match against the same-site rule or the exact trusted HTTPS origin, and any other target falls back. An explicit same-site path rule (for example: starts with one `/` but not `//` or `/\`) counts as a positive match.

items.key_phrase: Do not roll your own auth, crypto, token validation, sanitization, CSRF, parsers, or signature schemes.
items.look_at: How `src/redirect.js` reads the scheme and host of an absolute target
items.no_when: The scheme or host is extracted or matched with a regular expression, `split`, `indexOf`, or a hand-written parser.
items.question: Are absolute targets parsed with the platform `URL` parser and judged by its parsed `protocol` and host (or `origin`), rather than by regular expressions or string slicing on the raw target?
items.yes_when: The code builds a `URL` and compares its parsed fields.

items.key_phrase: Treat input that crosses a trust boundary as untrusted
items.look_at: The same-site path branch in `src/redirect.js`
items.no_when: A target passes as same-site because it merely starts with `/`, so a form such as `/\host` or `/\t/host` gets through.
items.question: Does the same-site check reject targets that a browser would send off-site, including protocol-relative `//host`, backslash `/\host`, and paths with leading whitespace or control characters such as a tab before `//host`?
items.yes_when: Relative targets are resolved against the trusted origin and the result's origin is compared, or the check explicitly rejects `//`, `/\`, and whitespace or control characters.

items.key_phrase: A bug fix needs a regression test that fails before the fix, passes after, and stays in the suite.
items.look_at: Test files the diff adds or changes, compared with the original code
items.no_when: No test passes an untrusted absolute URL, or the assertion would also pass on the original `return target`.
items.question: Is there a test that reproduces an open redirect, such as `https://evil.example/` returned unchanged, and would fail on the original code?
items.yes_when: A test passes an absolute URL on an untrusted host and asserts the result is `/`.

items.key_phrase: Every custom guard (sanitizer, validator, prototype guard, redirect check, redaction helper, crypto wrapper) ships with a negative test that fails on the unguarded code and passes with the guard.
items.look_at: Test files the diff adds or changes
items.no_when: Fewer than two bypass forms are tested.
items.question: Do tests assert that at least two different bypass forms, such as a protocol-relative target (`//host/...`), a non-HTTPS URL for the trusted host, or a script URL (`javascript:...`), each fall back to `/`?
items.yes_when: At least two different bypass forms each have an assertion that they resolve to `/`.

items.key_phrase: Every custom guard (sanitizer, validator, prototype guard, redirect check, redaction helper, crypto wrapper) ships with a negative test that fails on the unguarded code and passes with the guard.
items.look_at: Test files the diff adds or changes
items.no_when: None of these, or only one, is tested.
items.question: Do tests cover look-alike hosts and parser tricks: the trusted host as a prefix or suffix of another host, the trusted host as userinfo (`https://trusted@evil/`), and a backslash form (`/\host`)?
items.yes_when: Tests assert `/` for a prefix or suffix look-alike, a userinfo look-alike, and a backslash form.

items.key_phrase: Each test asserts a business rule from the acceptance criteria or spec, with expected values taken from there, not from the code.
items.look_at: Test files the diff adds or changes
items.no_when: Only rejections are tested, or an accepted target is checked only for not being `/`.
items.question: Does at least one test assert that a same-site path such as `/account/settings` is returned unchanged and that an HTTPS URL on the trusted host is accepted?
items.yes_when: Tests check both a same-site path and a trusted-host HTTPS URL against their expected returned values.

items.key_phrase: Every public operation that can fail has at least one failure-path test.
items.look_at: Public operations in the diff and the tests that call them
items.no_when: Only well-formed targets are tested.
items.question: Does a test pass a malformed target (an unparseable URL such as `https://` or `http://[`, or a non-string value) and assert it falls back to `/`?
items.yes_when: A test drives a malformed or non-string target and asserts `/`.

items.key_phrase: Never edit, skip, weaken, or delete a test, golden file, or snapshot to make the change pass.
items.look_at: Changes to test files that existed before the change
items.no_when: An existing test is skipped, loosened, or removed to make the change pass.
items.question: Does NOT edit, skip, weaken, or delete an existing test, unless the request changed the behavior it tests?
items.yes_when: Existing tests are unchanged, each change follows a behavior change the request made, or a test of internals is replaced by a test of the same rule.

items.key_phrase: Report what needs their attention first
items.look_at: The agent's final message
items.no_when: The chosen host is not mentioned, or is mentioned without saying it is an assumption that needs confirming.
items.question: Does the final message name the host it treated as the trusted app host and say the request did not name one, so the user must confirm or replace it?
items.yes_when: The message names the chosen trusted host as a placeholder or assumption and asks the user to confirm or set the real one, wherever it appears.

items.key_phrase: List each acceptance criterion with its check and result
items.look_at: The agent's final message, compared with the task's four requirements: same-site redirects kept, only the trusted HTTPS host for absolute redirects, malformed or suspicious targets fall back to `/`, and an explicit, auditable boundary
items.no_when: Some requirements go unmentioned, or the message only says that tests pass without tying them to the requirements.
items.question: For each of the request's requirements, does the final message say whether it was checked and how, or say that it was not checked?
items.yes_when: Every requirement is covered, in any wording or format, with how it was checked or a plain statement that it was not.

items.key_phrase: what proves it
items.look_at: Tests and files named in the agent's final message, compared with the final workspace
items.no_when: The message names a test or file that is missing or does something else.
items.question: Does every test and file the final message names exist in the diff or the repository, and do what the message says?
items.yes_when: Each named test and file exists and does what the message says.
